finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint sends an unauthenticated, caller-supplied URL to httpx. The only host check is a suffix match with no dot boundary, and nothing blocks private, loopback, or link-local addresses after DNS resolution. An attacker can reach internal hosts or cloud metadata through a domain they control, such as evilexample.com, that resolves to an internal IP. Only len(r.text) is returned, so this is a blind-equivalent SSRF, MEDIUM severity.
finding.source: mirror.py:11 - url query parameter in def mirror(url: str), unauthenticated route @app.get("/mirror")
finding.sink: mirror.py:16 - await c.get(url) via httpx.AsyncClient, using the raw caller string

trace.note: url enters from the query string on the unauthenticated GET /mirror route
host.endswith("example.com") is the only gate; it has no dot boundary, so evilexample.com and attackerexample.com pass
httpx.AsyncClient() is created with default settings: no IP/private-range blocking and no explicit follow_redirects=False
c.get(url) dispatches the request to the original caller-supplied URL, not to a validated, pinned host
return {"len": len(r.text)} exposes response size only, a length oracle for port scanning and service probing

finding.guards_checked: Scheme: httpx accepts only http/https, so file:// and gopher:// are rejected by the client; not a bypass. Host: suffix-only endswith check, not strict set membership, so it does not close the finding; ALLOWED_SUFFIX (line 7) is defined but never used. Resolved IP: no check for loopback, RFC-1918, link-local, or metadata addresses. Redirects: httpx defaults to follow_redirects=False since 0.20, so redirect-based bypass is not established; the installed httpx version was not confirmed. Port: unrestricted. Authentication: none on the route. The /ping handler (mirror.py:20-24) uses a hardcoded URL and is not a finding. A possible urlparse-vs-httpx parser differential was not tested (shell approval was blocked) and is not reported.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only host check is mirror.py:13, `host.endswith("example.com")`, a suffix match with no dot boundary, so it does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is defined but never used. There is no private, loopback, or link-local IP check, and the route at mirror.py:10 has no authentication.
verdict.reason: The caller-controlled `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) passes only the suffix check at mirror.py:13 and is then fetched unvalidated by `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16, so an attacker can use a domain such as evilexample.com that resolves to an internal address; the response length is returned at mirror.py:17. Every trace line matches the file.
